newsitem.title: USA: Mother of three allegedly burns home to hide fraud.
newsitem.headline: Mother of three allegedly burns home to hide fraud.

text.p: A woman allegedly set fire to her own home as her three children slept inside in a bizarre attempt to cover up a $20,000 embezzlement scheme, authorities said Friday.

Andrea Coverson, 28, was arrested Thursday when she was released from a hospital where she was treated for second-degree burns on her face, neck, hands, arms and abdomen. Police said she suffered the burns when she used gasoline to set fire to a bank night deposit vault in an effort to conceal $20,000 in cash she took from the weekend deposit of a convenience store she managed.

When Coverson struck a match to burn the vault's contents so it would appear the missing cash had been burned, vapours from the gasoline ignited, burning her and damaging her car but leaving the vault contents unharmed, authorities said.

In an attempt to explain the burns, Coverson allegedly set fire to the couch in her rented house after first arranging with another person to rescue her children, ages 10, 7 and 6 weeks, and take them to safety.

"She claimed she was asleep on the couch in this residence and woke up to being burned," said Butch Browning, East Baton Rouge Parish Arson Task Force director. "The fact that someone would go to that extreme to steal money, to put their family in danger ... that's probably the thing that is most disturbing," he said.

Coverson was booked into the parish prison Thursday night on charges of arson with intent to defraud, three counts of aggravated arson and two of felony theft, authorities said. The scheme unravelled when arson investigators working on both the house and bank fires noticed that Coverson had signed the deposit slips where cash was missing.
